residueConditions.name: Pristine / Factory Fresh or After Chemical Degreasing
residueConditions.description: Completely clean heating element, fan cowl, and upper chamber. Zero baked-on polymer varnish. Emitted aerosols originate solely from currently cooked food ingredients.

residueConditions.name: Light Organic Film (3–5 Cooking Cycles Without Wiping)
residueConditions.smokeGeneration: Low (Faint haze noticeable in small kitchens)
residueConditions.description: Thin lipid patina deposited from aerosolized spatter. Triglycerides have partially oxidized and adhered to the heating coil, beginning thermal decomposition upon subsequent heating.

residueConditions.name: Moderate Carbonized Varnish (10–20 Cycles Uncleaned)
residueConditions.elementColor: Dark amber to brown sticky hardened resin
residueConditions.description: Thick caramelized grease layer on heating coil and fan blades. Rapid beta-scission of fatty acids generates pungent acrolein and polycyclic aromatic hydrocarbon (PAH) vapors as high-speed convection air resuspends aerosolized soot.

residueConditions.name: Heavy Charred Slag (30+ Cycles Uncleaned / Dripping Coil)
residueConditions.elementColor: Black flaky blistered carbon crust with active tar buildup
residueConditions.description: Severely degraded, carbonized grease crust directly encasing the nichrome coils. Pyrolysis occurs continuously regardless of what food is being cooked, releasing severe spikes of Benzo[a]pyrene, chrysene, acrolein, and ultrafine PM2.5.

oilPrecursorTypes.name: Animal Tallow / Bacon / Poultry Schmaltz Residue
oilPrecursorTypes.description: High in cholesterol and saturated fatty acids. Thermal degradation creates dense carbonaceous soot particles laden with heavy polycyclic aromatic hydrocarbons (4-to-6 ring PAHs) that linger in indoor air.

oilPrecursorTypes.name: Polyunsaturated Seed Oils (Canola, Soybean, Corn Oil)
oilPrecursorTypes.description: Extremely vulnerable to free-radical lipid peroxidation. High linoleic acid content undergoes rapid oxidative cleavage into volatile cytotoxic aldehydes (acrolein, crotonaldehyde, 4-HNE) that severely irritate respiratory mucosa.

oilPrecursorTypes.name: Sugar & Protein Glaze (BBQ / Teriyaki / Honey-Glazed Spatter)
oilPrecursorTypes.description: Sugars and amino acids scorch rapidly at temperatures as low as 160°C. Generates intense visible smoke, sweet-acrid vapors, heterocyclic amines, and volatile furans that trigger immediate throat tickling and eye stinging.

oilPrecursorTypes.name: High-Oleic Extra Virgin Olive / Avocado Oil Residue
oilPrecursorTypes.dominantToxicants: Oleic acid fragmentation products, trace low-molecular-weight PAHs
oilPrecursorTypes.description: Natural polyphenolic antioxidants and single double-bond monounsaturated oleic chains confer high oxidative stability, delaying radical cleavage and resulting in lower volatile toxicant yields under moderate heat.

cookingTemperatures.kineticAerosolizationRate: Low (Gentle thermal evaporation, minimal bond cleavage)
cookingTemperatures.typicalFoods: Dehydrating fruits, slow reheating pastries, delicate warming

cookingTemperatures.kineticAerosolizationRate: Moderate (Initial lipid thermal oxidation and smoke release)
cookingTemperatures.typicalFoods: Baking muffins, roasting vegetables, chicken breast reheating

cookingTemperatures.kineticAerosolizationRate: High (Vigorous pyrolytic cracking, dense particulate plume)
cookingTemperatures.typicalFoods: Air-fried french fries, chicken wings, mozzarella sticks, frozen nuggets

cookingTemperatures.kineticAerosolizationRate: Extreme (Flash pyrolytic carbonization, heavy blue haze)
cookingTemperatures.typicalFoods: Max-crisp steak searing, sausage browning, blackened pork belly

ventilationModes.name: Ducted Range Hood Exhaust to Outdoors (>350 CFM)
ventilationModes.description: Optimal mitigation. High-velocity capture canopy pulls 90% of emitted particles and volatile PAHs outdoors before they disperse into the living space.

ventilationModes.name: Ductless Recirculating Range Hood (Charcoal Filter)
ventilationModes.description: Standard apartment setup. Metal grease mesh catches coarse oil droplets, but 65% of ultrafine PM2.5 and gaseous PAHs blow straight back into the room through the recirculating louvers.

ventilationModes.name: Natural Cross-Ventilation (Open Kitchen Window / Cross-Breeze)
ventilationModes.description: Moderate passive dilution. Dilutes aerosol concentrations over 15–30 minutes, but still exposes occupants in the kitchen to direct thermal plumes.

ventilationModes.name: Sealed / Closed Kitchen (Windows Shut, Exhaust Fan Off)
ventilationModes.description: High-risk scenario. Emitted ultrafine particles and PAHs accumulate unimpeded, recirculating through the HVAC system and remaining suspended for 2 to 4 hours.

deepCleaningProtocols.name: Unplug & Complete Cool-Down
deepCleaningProtocols.action: Ensure the appliance is fully unplugged from mains electricity and cooled to ambient room temperature before inspection.

deepCleaningProtocols.name: Inverted Inspection with Flashlight
deepCleaningProtocols.action: Flip the appliance upside down onto a soft kitchen towel. Use a flashlight to inspect the nichrome coil and behind the fan blades for brown varnish or carbon slag.

deepCleaningProtocols.name: Non-Abrasive Baking Soda Paste Application
deepCleaningProtocols.action: Mix 3 tablespoons baking soda with 1 tablespoon water and 1 teaspoon dish soap. Apply gently to the cold coil with a soft-bristle toothbrush. Avoid soaking the central motor shaft.

deepCleaningProtocols.name: Soft Steam Release Cycle
deepCleaningProtocols.action: Place an oven-safe ceramic bowl with 1 cup water and 2 lemon slices into the basket. Run at 180°C (350°F) for 5 minutes. The hot steam softens baked grease before final microfiber wipe-down.

deepCleaningProtocols.name: Always Position Air Fryer Under Active Exhaust
deepCleaningProtocols.action: Operate the air fryer directly on the stovetop beneath a running range hood ducted outdoors to capture high-velocity convection discharge.
